prediction.likelyOutcome: The landlord should prevail on liability outright (default, notices, non-cure, and judicial-process eviction are all well-documented) and should recover the core $783,504.15 unpaid-rent figure close to in full, plus the small utility/other charges. The $2.5 million 'security deposit replenishment' claim and the additional rent that accrued between the complaint and trial are the real variables -- the former turns on an unverified lease clause and double-counting risk, the latter on an undeveloped mitigation record -- so the net award will likely land well below the sum of everything pled, even though the landlord wins on liability across the board.

outcome.description: After a non-jury trial the court entered judgment for the landlord for $223,000, the rent due through July 1, 2022 when it regained possession, holding the tenant had been evicted (not abandoned) so the landlord could not recover post-possession rent; it denied the landlord's post-trial claim to $2,149,435.75 in actual damages. The Superior Court affirmed.
